keyTerms.definition: The instructors of the CS229 foundations course.
Each set changes one constraint on a taught mechanism.

recall.question: What is this file?
recall.answer: Ten transfer sets (T01-T10). Each changes one constraint on a mechanism taught in the course and asks the learner to transfer. Keys in keys-transfer.md.

sections.title: T01: LMS with a broken sensor (U02)

keyTerms.definition: One feature's sensor freezes halfway through training.
What happens to the gradient contribution; the normal equations; per-coordinate rates.

recall.question: T01: What are the answers?
recall.answer: (a) The update keeps moving on pure error feedback; the feature degrades into a second bias term. (b) X^T X gains a near-collinear column with the bias term.

sections.title: T02: Logistic regression under label shift (U03)

keyTerms.definition: Spam is 10x rarer, but p(x|y) is unchanged.
Which parameters stay valid; the Bayes correction; reweighting.

recall.question: T02: What are the answers?
recall.answer: (a) w stays valid; the intercept b must change. (b) logit p_new(y=1|x) = w^T x + b + log(pi_new/pi_old) - log((1-pi_new)/(1-pi_old)).

keyTerms.definition: Class 1 contains 20% mislabeled class-0 points.
How mu_1, Sigma, and the boundary move.

recall.question: T03: What are the answers?
recall.answer: (a) mu_1 moves toward mu_0: 0.8 mu_1 + 0.2 mu_0. (b) Sigma inflates. (c) The boundary shifts toward class 1's true region.

sections.title: T04: Kernel SVM on a budget (U05/U06)

keyTerms.definition: 1M points; O(n^2) once but never O(n^3).
SMO sweep cost; the approximation; the decision rule.

recall.question: T04: What are the answers?
recall.answer: (a) One SMO sweep is O(n^2) with O(n^2) memory: 8 TB. (b) Nystrom or random Fourier features.

sections.title: T05: Backprop with a dead branch (U07)

keyTerms.definition: One residual branch's weights freeze at init.
Forward, backward, and the gradient check.

recall.question: T05: What are the answers?
recall.answer: (a) y = x + F_frozen(x): a shallower model plus fixed random features. (b) The gradient is a random projection of the upstream gradient.

keyTerms.definition: Demonstrate double descent with real data and linear regression.
The design, the curves, the ridge response.

recall.question: T06: What are the answers?
recall.answer: (a) Fix n, vary d, fit ridgeless least squares. (b) Test error falls, spikes at d = n, falls again. (c) Optimal ridge flattens the peak.

sections.title: T07: Diffusion with a wrong schedule (U12)

keyTerms.definition: alpha-bar hits 0 at t = T/2 instead of T.
What x_{T/2} looks like; the ELBO terms; the samples.

recall.question: T07: What are the answers?
recall.answer: (a) Pure noise at T/2. (b) For t > T/2 the denoising targets are noise-predicting-noise. (c) Samples look like partial denoises, blurry or washed out.

sections.title: T08: RLVR with a helpful verifier (U15)

keyTerms.definition: The verifier accepts anything passing the public tests.
What the policy learns; whether the KL penalty saves you.

recall.question: T08: What are the answers?
recall.answer: (a) It learns to pass the public tests with minimal effort: reward hacking. (b) No: the KL penalty limits drift, not whether the destination is right.

keyTerms.definition: Actions take effect one time step late.
Why LQR breaks; the state augmentation.

recall.question: T09: What are the answers?
recall.answer: (a) The control authority matrix is zero at the current step: a_t = 0, which is wrong. (b) Augment the state with the previous action: new A = [[A, B],[0, 0]], new B = [[0],[I]].

keyTerms.definition: One large batch, 50 epochs, eps = 0.2.
The likelihood ratios; why the surrogate misleads; the two numbers.

recall.question: T10: What are the answers?
recall.answer: (a) Ratios explode on rare actions, collapse toward 0. (b) The surrogate is local to theta_old; after many epochs it optimizes a fiction. (c) KL(theta || theta_old) and the clipped fraction.
